metadata.agent_last_message:
Implemented the Rust CLI project in [`output/Cargo.toml`](/workspace/output/Cargo.toml) and [`output/src/main.rs`](/workspace/output/src/main.rs). The binary is `ical`, uses only the standard library, supports `parse` and `expand`, emits the required JSON shapes, handles the major component/property schemas, recurrence expansion, override processing, in-file `VTIMEZONE` resolution, warning kinds, and exit-1 error JSON.

`cargo build --release --manifest-path /workspace/output/Cargo.toml` succeeds. I also smoke-tested `parse`, `expand`, unresolved `TZID` handling, `THISANDFUTURE` overrides, and malformed `DTSTART` exit-1 behavior. Non-Gregorian `RSCALE` is parsed and surfaced; expansion warns with `rscale_unsupported` when the calendar scale is not supported for concrete expansion.

    def test_yearend_gap_detected_via_neighbor_year_scan(
        submission_command: tuple[str, ...], tmp_path: Path
    ) -> None:
        """Proves detect_tz_anomaly's (y-1, y, y+1) scan, not just year-y.
    
        Fixture: +00:00 → +01:00 spring-forward at local 2025-12-31 23:30.
        The gap runs [2025-12-31 23:30, 2026-01-01 00:30). An event at
        local 2026-01-01 00:15 is INSIDE the gap — but the transition is
        anchored to Dec 31 of the PRIOR year (2025). A detector that
        enumerates only the event's own year (2026) would generate the
        Dec 31 2026 23:30 transition, which is nowhere near the event.
        Catching this event requires scanning year 2025 (i.e. event.year - 1).
    
        If this test fails, the multi-year scan regressed to single-year."""
        body = (
            "UID:e-yearend\nDTSTAMP:20260101T120000Z\n"
            # Local 2026-01-01 00:15 lies in the 2025-12-31T23:30 +01:00 gap.
            "DTSTART;TZID=Test/YearEndGap:20260101T001500\n"
        )
        out = run_expand(
            submission_command,
            _wrap_yearend_tz(body),
            "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
            "2026-01-02T00:00:00Z",
            tmp_path,
        )

    def test_rrule_count_and_until_mutually_exclusive(
        submission_command: tuple[str, ...], tmp_path: Path
    ) -> None:
        """RFC 5545 §3.3.10: UNTIL and COUNT MUST NOT occur in the same
        'recur' part. When an RRULE carries both, the parser emits a
        `malformed_value` warning. We parse both keys so the raw RRULE
        round-trips in the JSON (downstream tooling can inspect the
